title: Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa
hook: a king who lost everything gets a guard at his door, and a visit home that Kerala gets ready for

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa brought us Bali's choice: warned by his teacher, he kept his word and offered his head for the third step. Did a small promise get kept? Day one thousand three hundred ninety-six.

Where do you send a king who has just lost the three worlds? We left Bali bound, his head under the foot of the giant Vamana. A story could end there, with the proud one humbled. The Bhagavata Purana doesn't. And Kerala doesn't either. On an Onam morning in Kerala, someone is on their knees at the front door, laying flower petals into a circle, ring by ring. In the way Kerala tells it, they're getting ready for a guest. Today, what happened to Bali next, and who the flowers are for.
screen: `BALI BOUND` → `FLOWERS BEFORE DAWN` → `READY FOR A GUEST`

segments.voice: First, the reward. In the Bhagavata, Bali's grandfather Prahlada arrives, and Bali's wife pleads for him. And Vishnu explains himself. Taking a person's wealth, he says, can be a kind of grace, because it frees them. Then he gives Bali a new home, a realm under the earth called Sutala, a place of comfort and peace. And he makes a startling promise. He will be there himself, standing at Bali's door with his mace in his hand, guarding him. The god who took the worlds becomes the doorkeeper of the king who gave them. Second, the visit. Here Kerala adds what the Bhagavata doesn't say. Tradition in Kerala says Bali asked for one more thing: to come back and see his people once a year. Onam is that visit. The king who once made the land fair comes up to look at it again. Third, the welcome. So people get ready the way you'd get ready for someone you love. The flower carpet at the door is the pookalam. The great meal, the sadya, is served on a banana leaf, with dish after dish set out in its place, and families sit down together to eat it. New clothes, games, boat races on the rivers, songs. Not because a god demands it, but because a beloved king is coming to see whether his people are still well. Put the pieces together and Onam says something unusual. Losing the throne wasn't the end of Bali. It's the reason he's remembered. If someone you loved came back to check on you, what would you want them to find?
screen: `SUTALA: A NEW HOME FOR BALI` · `VISHNU GUARDS BALI'S DOOR` · `ONE VISIT HOME A YEAR` · `FLOWERS, A FEAST, A WELCOME`

segments.voice: Lay a flower circle in the mind. Sit, and breathe slowly. With each breath, lay down one ring of petals, the way a pookalam is built, from the center out. One ring for the people in your home. One for your street. One for someone you haven't seen in a long time. Keep going, ring by ring, until the circle feels wide enough. Then rest in the middle of it. The bell holds the time.
Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa. Today, Bali's reward: Vishnu guards his door, and Kerala welcomes him home each Onam with flowers and a feast. Today's word.
Your line: Kerala's Onam and Ayyappa. Today, make one corner of your home ready for a guest, even if nobody's coming. Notice how it changes the room. Day one thousand three hundred ninety-six.

howItsDone: At Onam, families in Kerala lay a pookalam of flower petals at the door, wear new clothes and share the sadya, a feast served on a banana leaf, to welcome Mahabali on his visit to his people.
